title: Metabolism
hook: Every breath, heartbeat, and thought runs on metabolism — the vast web of chemical reactions that builds your body up and breaks your fuel down.
key_points: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions that keep an organism alive.
Catabolism breaks molecules down, releasing energy.
Anabolism builds complex molecules, using energy.
Enzymes guide these reactions, and ATP shuttles energy between them.
content_html: Metabolism is the chemistry of being alive — the entire, interlocking set of reactions a cell or body runs to grow, repair itself, move, and stay organized against the pull toward disorder. It's easy to think of metabolism only as "how fast you burn calories," but biologically it's far bigger: it's every chemical transformation happening in you at once, organized into pathways that hand products from one reaction to the next.
extra_html: Those reactions split into two complementary halves. Catabolism breaks large molecules — sugars, fats, proteins — into smaller pieces, releasing energy in the process; digesting a meal and cellular respiration are catabolic. Anabolism runs the other way, spending energy to assemble complex molecules like proteins, DNA, and new tissue. The two are linked by ATP, which captures energy freed during catabolism and delivers it to power anabolism, while enzymes catalyze nearly every step so the whole network runs at the right speed. As Encyclopaedia Britannica describes, this balance of building up and breaking down is what lets living things sustain themselves moment to moment.

related.title: ATP: The Cell's Energy Currency
related.hook: Cells don't store usable energy as sugar or fat alone — they spend it through ATP, a tiny rechargeable molecule that powers almost everything they do.

related.title: Enzymes: Life's Catalysts
related.hook: The chemical reactions that keep you alive would crawl too slowly to matter — enzymes speed them up millions of times without being used up themselves.

related.title: Cellular Respiration
related.hook: Every cell in your body slowly 'burns' sugar with oxygen to release energy — the same chemistry as photosynthesis, run in reverse.

flashcards.back_html: The entire web of chemical reactions that keep an organism alive — both the reactions that break molecules down and those that build them up.

flashcards.prompt: What is the difference between catabolism and anabolism?

choices.text: Catabolism breaks molecules down and releases energy; anabolism builds them up and uses energy
Catabolism builds molecules; anabolism destroys them
They are two words for the exact same process

flashcards.explanation_html: Catabolic reactions tear larger molecules apart, freeing energy (like digesting food); anabolic reactions spend that energy to construct complex molecules (like building proteins).

flashcards.prompt: What ties metabolism's two halves together?

choices.text: Energy released by catabolism is captured in ATP and spent on anabolism
Anabolism powers itself with no energy source

flashcards.explanation_html: Catabolism harvests energy from fuel into ATP, and anabolism spends that ATP to build the molecules a cell needs — enzymes steer every step of the loop.
